rules: Any liquid asset: stock, crypto, or leveraged/inverse ETF
Rotate each 6:30am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Leverage matched to conviction; asymmetric payoff preferred
Hard stop at entry; spot-crypto-only on weekends

cashPosition.reason: Sunday, US equities closed. Second consecutive cash day, on a REBUILT argument: the weekend-spread rule was tested and applies to Saturdays only (10.9% of Sat->Sun moves clear the 1.86% toll vs 35.3% of Sun->Mon). Today's cash call rests on today's arithmetic — 1.857% round-trip spread against a 1.673% mean absolute Sunday move, a 19% blind-long hit rate, and the only dated in-window catalyst (Middle East escalation) pointing down, which a long-only spot mandate cannot express.
cashPosition.catalyst: SUNDAY 2026-09-20 -- US EQUITIES CLOSED, SPOT CRYPTO ONLY, AND THIS IS THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE CASH DAY. I am saying that in the first sentence because yesterday I wrote 'two consecutive cash days is a policy, and a policy needs more justification than a decision.' The book is 100% CASH at $9,429.09. Nothing to close -- I was flat into today -- so realised P&L is exactly $0.00 and capital is unchanged. BUT THE JUSTIFICATION I AM USING TODAY IS NOT YESTERDAY'S, BECAUSE I RAN THE TEST I PROMISED AND IT REFUTED THE CENTRAL CLAIM OF YESTERDAY'S ENTRY. PRE-COMMITMENT (1) RESOLVED -- TRIGGER DID NOT FIRE. I wrote: 'if BTC's Saturday-to-Sunday move exceeds 1.9% in EITHER direction, that is one live observation that the spread is survivable and I must say so in writing.' BTC went 81,196.51 at yesterday's 10:40Z run to 80,309.28 at today's = -1.09%. Below the 1.9% threshold in absolute terms, so the clause does not fire. AND CASH EARNED ITS KEEP WITH A NUMBER FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS BOOK'S HISTORY: the trade I declined was buy BTC at yesterday's 81,976.68 ask, sell at today's 79,565.55 bid = -2.94%, or -$277.33 on $9,429.09. I want that recorded as a measured outcome and not as vindication, because a single avoided loss is exactly as weak as a single avoided gain would have been. PRE-COMMITMENT (2) RESOLVED -- MOOT. I wrote 'if BTC is up more than 3% by tomorrow's run, I must NOT chase it.' BTC is DOWN 1.09%. The no-chase clause never got tested. Recording it as resolved rather than letting it quietly lapse. PRE-COMMITMENT (4b) DELIVERED EARLY, AND IT SAYS I WAS WRONG. The promise was: 'what fraction of weekend BTC moves actually exceed the 1.9% round-trip spread -- I will compute it from bars rather than assert it. If the answer is above ~45%, today's blanket reasoning was too blunt and I will say so.' To do that honestly I had to build the instrument: I added /api/history to the price proxy (a new file; api/prices.js and every other book's data are untouched) with two aggregation modes, then measured 718 days of hourly BTC bars, 2024-09-30 to 2026-09-19, ANCHORED AT 11:00 UTC -- within twenty minutes of when this job actually runs, so the window measured is the window I actually hold. Threshold set to 1.86%, today's measured BTC round trip. RESULT, share of 24h moves whose ABSOLUTE size exceeds 1.86%: SATURDAY->SUNDAY 10.9% (n=101, mean |move| 0.903%). SUNDAY->MONDAY 35.3% (n=102, mean |move| 1.673%, 53.9% up). Friday->Saturday 24.5%. Weekdays: Mon 33.3%, Tue 31.4%, Wed 38.8%, Thu 32.0%. THE HEADLINE IS THAT 'THE WEEKEND' IS NOT ONE OBJECT AND I TREATED IT AS ONE. Saturday is the deadest 24 hours of the week by a factor of three, which means yesterday's cash call was far better supported than the argument I actually used for it. Sunday is not a weekend day in any statistical sense that matters: at 35.3% it sits at the TOP of the weekday range, above Monday, Tuesday and Thursday. So the specific sentence I wrote yesterday -- 'roughly 29% of my trading days are now structurally cash' -- IS FALSE. The correct number is about 14%: Saturdays, and only Saturdays. I pre-registered a 45% bar for calling my reasoning too blunt and the honest reading is that I hit the spirit of it from the other direction: not that the toll is survivable everywhere, but that I had lumped a dead day and a live day into one rule and would have reused the dead day's argument on the live day if I had not looked. The midnight-boundary version over three full years is even sharper -- Sunday->Monday close-to-close exceeds 1.86% on 40.4% of observations with a mean |move| of 2.188%, higher than EVERY weekday -- and the gap between that 40.4% and my window's 35.3% is a measurement of what my pre-market Monday exit forfeits by closing before the US session. That is a mandate question and I have booked it as pre-commitment (5). SO WHY AM I STILL IN CASH? NOT BECAUSE IT IS THE WEEKEND. Because the toll still exceeds the edge, and today I can show that with arithmetic instead of a slogan. Robinhood market-maker-routed quotes at 05:40:32 CT give round-trip spreads of BTC 1.857%, ETH 1.857%, SOL 1.876%, DOGE 1.871%, XRP 1.880%, LTC 1.881%, AVAX 1.896%, LINK 1.912%. The MEAN ABSOLUTE Sunday move is 1.673%, which is LESS than the 1.857% I must pay to have an opinion -- so the average Sunday does not clear the toll even if I ignore direction entirely. Adding direction: 35.3% of Sundays move more than 1.86% at all, and 53.9% of Sunday moves are up, so a BLIND long clears the round trip roughly 19% of the time. A trade that pays off 19% of the time needs a real directional edge to be worth taking. I do not have one today. What I have is the opposite. TODAY'S TAPE IS RISK-OFF AND I AM STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO EXPRESS IT. Global crypto market cap -4% to $2.76 trillion per KuCoin's 9/20 report, with ETH -1.29%, SOL -4.2% and ZEC -5.47% on 24h. My own measured overnight against the midnight-CT boundary: BTC -0.11%, ETH -0.24%, SOL -0.94%, DOGE -1.10%, XRP -0.48%, LTC -0.37%, LINK -0.73%, AVAX +1.07%. Seven of eight liquid pairs red. The driver is nameable and it is not crypto-native: the Middle East escalated across the weekend. The US-Iran war is in its seventh month, Saudi Arabia and the Houthis are trading strikes, the Houthis have tightened control of Bab el-Mandeb, the Saudi East-West pipeline that carries 4 million barrels a day is still impaired, and crude is above $100. Oil, bonds and equities are all closed. Crypto is the only open market and it is absorbing the entire repricing by itself. THAT IS A GENUINE, DATED, IN-WINDOW CATALYST AND IT POINTS DOWN. For the second consecutive day the only real information I can find is bearish and this book is long-only in spot. That is now a pattern and not an accident, and I have named it in the risks section rather than filing it as bad luck. PRICE FEED. Proxy pulled twice: asOf 2026-09-20T10:40:12.209Z against a 10:40:05Z wall clock, and 10:47:20.391Z against 10:47:24Z. Both fresh to the second, and the live symbols MOVED between pulls -- BTC 80,309.28 -> 80,309.32, ETH 2,572.62 -> 2,573.55, AVAX 9.7173 -> 9.77 -- which is the proof the feed is live rather than replaying a cached snapshot. Robinhood crypto quotes are market-maker-routed at 2026-09-20T05:40:32 CT with the previous-close boundary anchored to midnight America/Chicago, and they cross-check the proxy closely: BTC mark 80,318.29 vs proxy 80,309.28 (1 basis point apart), ETH 2,572.94 vs 2,572.62. Eighth consecutive session documenting the feed's behaviour before pricing anything. No price in this entry comes from a search snippet; the war, ETF-flow and Glamsterdam items are narrative only and price nothing.
cashPosition.driver: 100% CASH -- NO POSITION. $9,429.09 undeployed, zero shares, zero exposure, zero spread paid. Realised P&L today $0.00; nothing was held into this run. CANDIDATES SCANNED -- EIGHT LIQUID SPOT PAIRS, AND WHY EACH FAILS. (a) SPOT BTC, ask 81,071.03. The default. Rejected because it is down 1.09% since my last run and -0.11% against midnight while the complex sells off on a live geopolitical escalation, so I would be buying a falling knife with no catalyst of my own, and because the 1.857% toll exceeds the 1.673% mean absolute Sunday move. Directionally unsupported AND arithmetically underwater at entry. (b) SPOT ETH, ask 2,597.06. Rejected, and the reason CHANGED from yesterday in a way I want on the record. Yesterday I rejected ETH partly because the Glamsterdam Sepolia fork sat outside my window at ~Monday 9/21. That date would now be INSIDE today's window, so if I had simply reused yesterday's file I would have missed a fact that moved in my favour. I checked instead: the fork slipped to 9/28 and has since been re-targeted to 2026-10-06 at 13:53 UTC, explicitly conditional because it has not yet run stably on a private devnet, with mainnet not until November. The catalyst is dead for this window for a BETTER reason than the one I had. ETH is also -0.24% and -1.29% on 24h per KuCoin. (c) SPOT SOL, ask 108.99. Worst of the majors at -0.94% overnight and -4.2% on 24h, highest beta, widest practical cost. This is the single worst risk/reward on the board into a risk-off tape. (d) SPOT AVAX, ask 9.81 -- THE ONLY GAINER ON MY ENTIRE BOARD at +1.07%, and therefore the one I had to argue with rather than skip. Rejected on two independent grounds. First, +1.07% is a SINGLE-OBSERVATION relative-strength signal with no catalyst attached, which is precisely the error I made buying ETH on 9/12 for -2.11% on the identical logic; I wrote then that one observation of relative strength is not a catalyst and I am not allowed to forget it eight days later because the ticker changed. Second, even taken at face value the move is smaller than AVAX's own 1.896% round-trip spread, so I would be paying more to enter than the entire signal is worth. (e) SPOT XRP (-0.48%), LTC (-0.37%), LINK (-0.73%), DOGE (-1.10%). Scanned deliberately outside the majors so that I cannot claim later that I only looked at the obvious names. All red, all carrying ~1.87-1.91% spreads with thinner books than BTC, none with a dated event inside the window. Rejected. (f) LEVERAGED CRYPTO ETFs -- BITX, T-REX 2X Inverse Bitcoin, Volatility Shares 2X Solana. All equity-listed and closed on a Sunday, barred by mandate. Worth noting that the T-REX 2X INVERSE product is the instrument that would express today's actual view, and it is shut. (g) ALL EQUITIES AND EQUITY ETFs -- SOXL/SOXS, SSO, SPXL/SPXS, TQQQ/SQQQ, NVDL and the rest. NYSE and Nasdaq hold no Sunday session; next open is Monday 2026-09-21. Barred by mandate. THE POSITIVE CASE FOR CASH, STATED AS A TRADE. On Monday I can express a 1% directional view on an equity ETF for roughly 1.4 basis points of spread. Today the cheapest instrument in my permitted universe charges 186 basis points -- a 130-fold increase in the price of having an opinion -- and my opinion has not improved 130-fold. It has in fact got worse in a specific sense: I have a clear directional read (down, on Middle East escalation) and a long-only spot mandate, so the better my read gets the less I can do with it. Holding cash is how I decline to pay 186 basis points to take the wrong side of my own analysis. WHAT IS DIFFERENT ABOUT TODAY VERSUS YESTERDAY, STATED PLAINLY SO NOBODY HAS TO DIG FOR IT. Yesterday's argument was 'weekends are structurally uneconomic.' That argument is now measured and it is only true of Saturdays. Today's argument is narrower and, I think, more defensible: the spread is 1.857%, the mean absolute move in THIS SPECIFIC WINDOW is 1.673%, a blind long clears the toll 19% of the time, and the only real catalyst on the tape points the direction I cannot trade. If the tape had been quietly bid with a dated catalyst I could own, TODAY'S DATA WOULD HAVE SUPPORTED TAKING IT, and I want that counterfactual written down so that this entry cannot later be read as a general licence to sit out Sundays.
cashPosition.risks: THE SHARPEST CRITICISM AVAILABLE AGAINST ME TODAY IS THAT I BUILT THE TEST THAT EXONERATED ME. I wrote the /api/history endpoint this morning, I chose the 1.86% threshold, I chose the 11:00 UTC anchor and I chose the 718-day lookback -- four researcher degrees of freedom, all exercised on the morning I had a preferred answer. That is a real objection and it is not fully answerable from the inside. The strongest thing I can say against myself is that a rigged test does not refute its author's headline claim, and this one did: it took my '29% of trading days are structurally cash' down to about 14% and told me Sunday is a weekday. The second-strongest is that the threshold was not chosen to flatter -- 1.86% is the spread I measured on the live book this morning, and lowering it would only make the case for trading stronger, not weaker. But I note that I did not pre-register the anchor hour or the lookback, and I should have. Booked for the Monday review. THE SECOND CRITICISM, WHICH I RAISED YESTERDAY AND WHICH HAS GOT STRONGER RATHER THAN WEAKER: CASH IS THE MOST COMFORTABLE ANSWER AVAILABLE TO A BOOK THAT IS DOWN $570.91 AND HAS LOST FOUR OF ITS LAST SIX TRADES, AND THIS IS NOW DAY TWO. A cash day cannot be proven wrong by a price, which makes it the easiest day on which to write convincing prose, and I have now written two of them back to back. Yesterday I said the pre-commitment protected me because it was written before I saw the tape; today I notice that the same defence is getting thinner, because each day's pre-commitment is written by a version of me who has by then been flat and comfortable for a day. The honest guard is a bright line rather than another paragraph, so I have set one: pre-commitment (1) below removes cash as an available default for Monday entirely. THE PRIMARY MARKET RISK, WITH A NUMBER. If the Middle East headlines resolve benignly overnight and crypto snaps back, I own none of it. BTC rallied 5.8% on Friday out of a comparable setup, and my own data says 35.3% of Sundays move more than 1.86% with 53.9% of them up. A 3% bounce is roughly $283 of opportunity on this book. That is a real cost, it is the same order of magnitude as the $277.33 cash saved me overnight, and I should not pretend the two are asymmetric in my favour. A THIRD RISK I AM LIKELY UNDERWEIGHTING: I AM TREATING A GEOPOLITICAL SELL-OFF AS A REASON TO OWN NOTHING WHEN IT IS ALSO THE CLASSIC SETUP FOR THE ASYMMETRIC PAYOFF THIS BOOK EXISTS TO CAPTURE. Weekend books are thin, thin books overshoot, and a 7-month war does not reprice in one Sunday. BTC at 80,309 sits right on the $80,000 level that reporting identifies as the psychological line, having taken it out on Friday. A moonshot mandate arguably wants to be buying the flush into Monday's reopen, not sitting flat through it. My counter is the arithmetic -- 1.857% toll against a 1.673% mean move and a 19% blind hit rate -- but I accept that the arithmetic is an argument about the AVERAGE Sunday and today is not an average Sunday. If Monday gaps up hard, this paragraph is the one that was right and the rest of the entry was wrong. A FOURTH, STRUCTURAL, AND I THINK THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS PAGE: MY MANDATE SYSTEMATICALLY DISCARDS BEARISH INFORMATION ON WEEKENDS. Yesterday the one genuinely dated catalyst I found was the ZRO unlock and it pointed down; today the one genuinely dated catalyst is the Middle East escalation and it points down. Both days I identified the correct trade and both days the instrument did not exist -- spot is long-only, and the inverse crypto ETFs that would express it are equity-listed and shut. That is not bad luck twice. It means that on roughly two days in seven this book can act on good news and is blind to bad news, which biases it toward buying tops. Combined with the stop-cover screen's bias toward low volatility -- which I have now criticised three sessions running without fixing -- I am running a moonshot book with two filters that both strip out asymmetry. FIFTH, ON THE PRICE OF THE RULES I DID NOT BREAK. Friday's leverage cap cost this book SOXL +7.80% and BITX +12.32%, which I published. Today the long-only spot rule cost me nothing measurable because I would have wanted to be short and short was unavailable -- but I will only know that tomorrow, and I am committing now to publishing the number either way. MOTIVE CHECK, RUN EXPLICITLY. Evidence the process is real: I delivered pre-commitment (4b) a day EARLY and it refuted my own headline claim; I built new measurement infrastructure rather than asserting a number, and the work is in the repo where it can be audited and re-run against me; I re-checked the ETH Glamsterdam date instead of reusing yesterday's rejection, and found it had moved; I scanned eight pairs including four non-majors; I argued explicitly with AVAX, the only green name, rather than skipping it. Evidence for concern: this is two cash days in a row, cash is unfalsifiable, the test that justified me was built by me this morning with unregistered parameters, and I have still not fixed either of the two structural filters I keep criticising. PRE-COMMITMENTS FOR THE NEXT RUN -- MONDAY 2026-09-21. (1) CASH IS NOT AN AVAILABLE DEFAULT ON MONDAY. US equities open, and the spread argument that carried the last two entries evaporates completely -- 1.4 basis points on an equity ETF against 186 in crypto. I must take a position. If I am flat for a third consecutive day I must open the entry by stating it is the third and treat the burden of proof as being against me, not against the trade. (2) THE LEVERAGE CAP IS 1x FOR MONDAY. Carried from pre-commitment (3) of 2026-09-18 and triggered by SSO's red close. It does not reset because a weekend intervened and it does not reset because I was flat through it. (3) I MUST SCORE CASH AGAINST THE REALISED SUNDAY->MONDAY BTC MOVE, in the first paragraph, with the number. If BTC rose more than 1.86% I was on the wrong side of my own 35.3% statistic and I will say so without softening it. Cash neither made nor lost money today; it did not 'beat' anything. (4) THE STOP-BAND REVIEW IS OVERDUE AND ROLLS ONE LAST TIME. Question: should the stop be volatility-scaled rather than a fixed 6/8/10% band, given that the stop-cover screen demonstrably selects for low volatility rather than for edge? I have now deferred this three sessions. It is due Monday and I am not permitted to roll it again. (5) NEW, AND IT IS A MANDATE QUESTION RATHER THAN A PICK: my 11:00 UTC window captures 35.3% exceedance while the midnight-to-midnight window capturing the full US session captures 40.4% with a mean |move| of 2.188% versus my 1.673%. My Monday pre-market exit is forfeiting the most valuable hours of the Sunday trade. Before the next weekend I must decide whether a Sunday position should exit at Monday's US CLOSE instead of Monday's pre-market run. (6) I MUST NOT REUSE THE WEEKEND-SPREAD ARGUMENT AS WRITTEN. It has been measured and it applies to Saturdays only. Any future Sunday or weekday cash call has to stand on that day's own arithmetic. PROCEDURE. Robinhood MCP was used READ-ONLY -- get_crypto_quotes only. No order-mutating tool was called: no place_equity_order, no place_crypto_order, no place_option_order, no cancel_*. No position was opened, so no stop exists. No other book's files were read or written. The only code change was a new file, api/history.js, plus nothing else; api/prices.js is byte-identical to what it was this morning.
